findings.title: Task 1's unindexed `[~]` fixture line cannot match the parser regex
findings.description:
Task 1 prescribes `7. [~] Feature Epsilon without explicit index — cut for scope.` and limits the bold-wrap requirement to "the indexed form". `PLAN_UNINDEXED_RE` requires `**Name**`, so this line still matches nothing after Task 2 widens the character class.

- **Effect:** Task 5's assertions (unindexed entry is `deprecated`/`fallback`, `totalSlices: 7`, `completedSlices: 5`) cannot pass.
- **Likely cause:** the example copies the non-bold shape of the "Future Work" line at `sample-slice-plan.md:32`, which a different parser consumes.
- **Fix:** use the slice design's stated form, `N. [~] **Name** — rationale`.

findings.title: Editing the shared fixture breaks existing tests the tasks do not update
findings.description:
Task 1 adds two entries to `sample-slice-plan.md`; Task 5 updates only the `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` test. Once the unindexed line is corrected to parse, these also break:

- **`slicePlanParser.test.ts:10`:** `toHaveLength(5)` fails.
- **`slicePlanParser.test.ts:12`, `:22`, `:166-167`:** the fallback entry gets index 1 and sorts first, so `entries[0]` is no longer 101 and `entries[2]` is no longer 103.
- **`slicePlanParser.test.ts:128`:** "every entry `indexSource: explicit`" fails because of the fallback entry.
- **`ArtifactIntrospector.test.ts:52`:** `totalSlices` `toBe(5)` fails.

This also contradicts the slice's last success criterion, which wants the existing `sample-slice-plan.md` tests "continuing to pass unchanged", and Task 5's own "byte-identical" regression sub-item.

**Fix:** put the `[~]` lines in a sibling fixture (the slice design allows "or add a sibling fixture") and leave `sample-slice-plan.md` and its tests untouched. Task 5's `totalSlices`/`completedSlices` rewrite then goes away.

findings.title: Task 8 misstates the caller of `resolveEntryStatus`; the `Pick` widening as written will not typecheck
findings.description: Task 8 says the only caller "passes a full `SlicePlanEntry`". The actual caller is `resolveEntryStatusSafe`, whose own parameter is `Pick<SlicePlanEntry, 'index' | 'isChecked'>`. Widening only `resolveEntryStatus` produces a compile error at line 740. The task should name both signatures.

findings.title: Task 9's `derivedStatus` initializer change is unjustified scope
findings.description: The slice design gives `slice.ts` a "one-line addition" to the `deriveEntryStatus` call. Task 9 also rewrites the initializer, reasoning that a `detectDocuments` failure would otherwise report `not-started`. That is wrong: the catch at `slice.ts:125-127` sets `derivedStatus = 'degraded'`, and the try path always reassigns. The initializer value never survives, so cut the sub-item.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkbox items
findings.description: All six commit lines are `- [ ] Commit: ...` sub-items (lines 105, 135, 179, 197, 212, 224). They should be plain `**Commit**:` lines, never checkboxes. Their placement is sound, each after a passing test task.

findings.title: Task count is heavy for the change, and Task 8's test lands after its commit
findings.description:
The production change is roughly ten lines across four files, spread over 13 tasks.

- **Merge:** Tasks 2, 3 and 4 are three small edits to one function in one file with one shared test task; make them one task.
- **Reorder:** Task 11 is the only test of Task 8's `WorkflowNavigator` wiring, but it follows the Task 10 commit that ships that wiring. Move it ahead of that commit and drop its separate commit.
- **Cut:** Task 5's "explicit regression test" sub-item duplicates the existing fixture tests once a sibling fixture is used.

findings.title: `arch-status-vs-plans` has no direct test
findings.description: The success criterion names both `plan-status-vs-entries` and `arch-status-vs-plans`; Task 12 tests only the first. The slice says both rules consume the same `completedSlices` value, so the arithmetic is covered indirectly. One extra arch-level case would close it, but it is not required.
